title: GrepSeek: Training Search Agents for Direct Corpus Interaction

visual_explainer.question: Can a compact model learn effective direct-corpus search behavior rather than relying on a frontier model to improvise shell interaction?
visual_explainer.takeaway: GrepSeek trains the DCI policy itself with verified cold-start trajectories followed by GRPO, while a sharded execution engine reduces shell-search cost without changing command semantics.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Prompted/frontier-model DCI and retriever-mediated Search-R1 baselines.

analysis.tldr: GrepSeek turns DCI from a frontier-model prompting result into a trainable search policy: verified cold-start trajectories initialize shell-search behavior, GRPO refines it, and sharded execution accelerates exact command evaluation.
analysis.problem: Raw DCI depends on a capable model discovering good shell-search behavior online, while direct RL over a large corpus is unstable and sequential shell scans are slow.
analysis.core_idea: Generate causally grounded search trajectories with an answer-aware tutor and answer-blind planner, train an initial policy with SFT, refine it with GRPO through direct corpus interaction, and execute shell commands across semantics-preserving shards in parallel.
analysis.agent_loop: reason → emit shell search/filter command → observe raw-corpus matches → refine constraints → compose evidence → answer
analysis.retrieval_design: The corpus remains the environment rather than a ranked top-k API; the learned object is the policy that chooses exact lexical/file operations.
analysis.evidence: Across seven QA benchmarks the paper reports a 0.5691 micro-average F1, above the strongest Search-R1 dense configuration at 0.5441, with significant overall improvement. SFT and GRPO ablations both degrade strongly. The sharded executor reduces average shell-search latency from 5.39s to 0.71s (up to 7.6×). A key negative result is PopQA, where GrepSeek is significantly worse than the best dense baseline because exact lexical matching is brittle to surface-form variation.
analysis.why_it_matters: It shows that the retrieval interface and the policy over that interface can be learned separately: DCI is not only a capability of expensive frontier harnesses. It also exposes the semantic tail where dense retrieval remains complementary.
limitations: Exact lexical interaction is brittle to paraphrases, diacritics, and overloaded keywords.
The end-to-end method bundles trajectory synthesis, SFT, RL, and an execution engine, so aggregate gains do not isolate one component.
The corpus interface remains file/text-centric; transfer to web/API/structured-data environments is open.
